subject: Science
title: Keeping clean and healthy
objectives: Children will wash hands and say when we wash them.
Children will practise brushing teeth with a model.
content: Washing hands, brushing teeth with a model, and healthy habits.
teachingActivities: Use real soap and water for hand washing; use a model mouth and a big toothbrush for teeth; sing a short washing song; model each step; make hand washing part of the daily routine.
learnerActivities: Wash hands with soap, practise brushing teeth with a model and name healthy habits.
resources: A teeth model and a large toothbrush
Glitter or flour to show germs
assessment: Observe whether each child washes hands with soap with support and says one healthy habit.
expectedOutcomes: Washes hands with soap with support.

lessons.title: Washing hands
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will wash their hands with soap and say when we wash them.
successCriteria: Says one time we wash hands
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have explored the senses, food and caring and have practised looking after living things.
resources: A picture of times to wash hands
lessons.starter: Show your dirty hands and say "My hands are dirty. We need to wash them."
teacherActivities: Show how to wet hands, rub with soap and rinse.
Sing a washing song while rubbing: "Rub, rub, rub your hands."
Dry hands on a clean towel.
learnerActivities: Children watch and copy the actions.
Child says after toilet or before eating.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show how to wet hands, rub with soap and rinse. Children: Children watch and copy the actions.
Step 2. Teacher: Sing a washing song while rubbing: "Rub, rub, rub your hands." Children: Children sing and rub.
Step 3. Teacher: Dry hands on a clean towel. Children: Child dries hands.
Step 4. Teacher: Ask "When do we wash hands?" Children: Child says after toilet or before eating.

practical.title: Hand washing
steps: Set up a basin, soap and towels.
practical.safety: Use mild soap and keep water shallow. Wipe spills quickly and supervise closely. Use a clean towel for each child.

differentiation.support: Wash hands together with a hand over the child’s hand.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to teach a friend how to wash hands.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Why do we wash hands?
questions.expected: To get clean and stay healthy.

questions.question: When do we wash hands?
questions.expected: Before eating and after the toilet.

expectedOutcomes: Washes hands with soap with support
lessons.conclusion: Show clean hands and say "Clean hands."
lessons.homeConnection: Wash hands together at home before meals and after the toilet.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "wash their hands with soap and say when we wash them" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

learnerFacing.songOrRhyme: Rub, rub, rub your hands. Wash, wash, wash away.

lessons.title: Brushing teeth
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will practise brushing teeth with a model.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have explored the senses, food and caring and have practised looking after living things.
lessons.starter: Show the teeth model and say "These are teeth. We brush them to keep them clean."
teacherActivities: Show how to brush the model teeth up and down and round.
Let each child brush the model teeth.
Look at your own teeth in the mirror.
Say "We brush in the morning and at night."
learnerActivities: Children watch and copy in the air.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show how to brush the model teeth up and down and round. Children: Children watch and copy in the air.
Step 2. Teacher: Let each child brush the model teeth. Children: Child brushes the model.
Step 3. Teacher: Look at your own teeth in the mirror. Children: Child looks and says teeth.
Step 4. Teacher: Say "We brush in the morning and at night." Children: Children say morning and night.

practical.title: Brush the teeth
steps: Look at your own teeth in a mirror.
practical.safety: Use only the model for brushing in class unless parents have agreed to supervised brushing with personal brushes. Never share toothbrushes.

differentiation.extension: Ask the child to say how long we should brush.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Smile and show your clean teeth.
lessons.homeConnection: Brush teeth together morning and night at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "practise brushing teeth with a model" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Healthy habits
lessons.subject: Science
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have explored the senses, food and caring and have practised looking after living things.
resources: Pictures: washing, brushing, sleeping, eating well, playing outside, drinking water
lessons.starter: Show a picture of washing hands and say "This is a healthy habit. It keeps us well."
teacherActivities: Show each picture and say the healthy habit.
Let each child choose a picture and act it.
learnerActivities: Children look and say the habit.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show each picture and say the healthy habit. Children: Children look and say the habit.
Step 2. Teacher: Act out each habit. Children: Children copy the actions.
Step 3. Teacher: Ask "How do we stay healthy?" Children: Child points to a picture.
Step 4. Teacher: Let each child choose a picture and act it. Children: Child acts and friends guess.

practical.title: Healthy habits
practical.safety: Keep the floor clear and supervise movement. Be sensitive to families’ different circumstances.

differentiation.support: Act together and say the habit.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to say which habit they do every day.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: How do we stay healthy?
questions.expected: Wash, sleep, eat well and play.

lessons.conclusion: Say "I am healthy" together and wave.
lessons.homeConnection: Talk about healthy habits at home each day.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "name healthy habits" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Germs and clean hands
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will see why washing hands with soap matters.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have explored the senses, food and caring and have practised looking after living things.
resources: Flour or a little washable paint on hands to show dirt
lessons.starter: Show hands with a little flour and say "These hands are dirty. How can we clean them?"
teacherActivities: Wash one hand with water only and one with soap.
Say "Soap helps to take away dirt and germs."
Let each child wash their own floury hands.
Say "Clean hands help us stay healthy."
learnerActivities: Child washes and sees clean hands.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Wash one hand with water only and one with soap. Children: Children watch what happens.
Step 2. Teacher: Say "Soap helps to take away dirt and germs." Children: Children say soap.
Step 3. Teacher: Let each child wash their own floury hands. Children: Child washes and sees clean hands.
Step 4. Teacher: Say "Clean hands help us stay healthy." Children: Children say the sentence.

practical.title: Clean hands test
steps: Put a little flour on hands.
Wash with water and then with soap.
practical.safety: Use only a little washable flour or paint and mild soap. Keep water shallow and wipe spills.

differentiation.support: Wash together and name each step.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to say why soap is better than water alone.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Show your clean hands and cheer.
lessons.homeConnection: Make hand washing a family routine.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "see why washing hands with soap matters" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Week 8 health check
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Teachers will observe how each child practises hygiene.
successCriteria: Washes hands with soap with support
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have explored the senses, food and caring and have practised looking after living things.
lessons.starter: Sing the washing song and show three stations.
teacherActivities: Set up three stations: hand washing, teeth and healthy habits.
At each station ask "What do we do?" and "Why?"
Record each child’s level and take photographs.
learnerActivities: Child answers with a word or action.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up three stations: hand washing, teeth and healthy habits. Children: Children rotate every four minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: At each station ask "What do we do?" and "Why?" Children: Child answers with a word or action.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level and take photographs. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Health stations
practical.safety: Supervise each station and wipe spills at once. Use mild soap and clean towels.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and use one station.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to explain hand washing to a friend.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: washes hands with soap; practises brushing; names healthy habits.

questions.question: When do we wash hands?
questions.expected: Before eating and after the toilet.

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 8
lessons.conclusion: Show clean hands and wave goodbye.
lessons.homeConnection: Practise hygiene routines every day at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will observe how each child practises hygiene" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?
